title: Quercetin and AMPK: A Dynamic Duo in Alleviating MG-Induced Inflammation via the AMPK/SIRT1/NF-kappaB Pathway.
authors: Lu, Ziyin; Wang, Haozhen; Ishfaq, Muhammad; Han, Yufang; Zhang, Xiujin; Li, Xiang; Wang, Baoqi; Lu, Xiuli; Gao, Bing
one_liner_zh: 该文研究槲皮素通过AMPK/SIRT1/NF-kappaB通路缓解禽支原体炎症，虽用AlphaFold2和分子对接，但核心是蛋白-小分子互作与信号通路，非蛋白质-DNA互作或TF-DNA结合体系，与本课题关联微弱。
abstract: Mycoplasma gallisepticum (MG) is recognized as a principal causative agent of avian chronic respiratory disease, inflicting substantial economic losses upon the poultry industry. However, the extensive use of conventional antibiotics has resulted in the emergence of drug resistance and various challenges in their clinical application. Consequently, there is an urgent need to identify effective therapeutic agents for the prevention and treatment of mycoplasma-induced respiratory disease in avian species. AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK) holds significant importance as a regulator of cellular energy metabolism and possesses the capacity to exert an anti-inflammatory effect by virtue of its downstream protein, SIRT1. This pathway has shown promise in counteracting the inflammatory responses triggered by pathogenic infections, thus providing a novel target for studying infectious inflammation. Quercetin possesses anti-inflammatory activity and has garnered attention as a potential alternative to antibiotics. However, there exists a gap in knowledge concerning the impact of this activation on MG-induced inflammatory damage. To address this knowledge gap, we employed AlphaFold2 prediction, molecular docking, and kinetic simulation methods to perform a systematic analysis. As expected, we found that both quercetin and the AMPK activator AICAR activate the chicken AMPKgamma1 subunit in a similar manner, which was further validated at the cellular level. Our project aims to unravel the underlying mechanisms of quercetin's action as an agonist of AMPK against the inflammatory damage induced by MG infection. Accordingly, we evaluated the effects of quercetin on the prevention and treatment of air sac injury, lung morphology, immunohistochemistry, AMPK/SIRT1/NF-kappaB pathway activity, and inflammatory factors in MG-infected chickens. The results confirmed that quercetin effectively inhibits the secretion of pro-inflammatory cytokines such as IL-1beta, TNF-alpha, and IL-6, leading to improved respiratory inflammation injury. Furthermore, quercetin was shown to enhance the levels of phosphorylated AMPK and SIRT1 while reducing the levels of phosphorylated P65 and pro-inflammatory factors. In conclusion, our study identifies the AMPK cascade signaling pathway as a novel cellular mediator responsible for quercetin's ability to counter MG-induced inflammatory damage. This finding highlights the potential significance of this pathway as an important target for anti-inflammatory drug research in the context of avian respiratory diseases.
abstract_zh: 鸡毒支原体（Mycoplasma gallisepticum, MG）被公认为禽类慢性呼吸道疾病的主要病原体，给家禽业造成重大经济损失。然而，传统抗生素的广泛使用已导致耐药性的出现及其临床应用中的多种挑战。因此，迫切需要寻找有效的治疗药物来预防和治疗禽类支原体引起的呼吸道疾病。AMP活化蛋白激酶（AMPK）作为细胞能量代谢的调节因子具有重要意义，并凭借其下游蛋白SIRT1具备抗炎作用的能力。该通路在对抗病原感染引发的炎症反应方面显示出潜力，从而为研究感染性炎症提供了新靶点。槲皮素具有抗炎活性，并作为抗生素的潜在替代品受到关注。然而，关于这种激活对MG诱导的炎症损伤的影响，目前存在知识空白。为填补这一空白，我们采用AlphaFold2预测、分子对接和动力学模拟方法进行了系统分析。如预期所料，我们发现槲皮素和AMPK激活剂AICAR以相似方式激活鸡AMPKgamma1亚基，这进一步在细胞水平得到验证。本项目旨在揭示槲皮素作为AMPK激动剂对抗MG感染诱导的炎症损伤的潜在机制。因此，我们评估了槲皮素对MG感染鸡气囊损伤预防和治疗、肺形态、免疫组织化学、AMPK/SIRT1/NF-kappaB通路活性及炎症因子的影响。结果证实，槲皮素有效抑制IL-1beta、TNF-alpha和IL-6等促炎细胞因子的分泌，从而改善呼吸道炎症损伤。此外，槲皮素被证明能提高磷酸化AMPK和SIRT1水平，同时降低磷酸化P65和促炎因子水平。总之，我们的研究将AMPK级联信号通路确定为槲皮素对抗MG诱导炎症损伤的新型细胞介质。这一发现突显了该通路作为禽类呼吸道疾病抗炎药物研究重要靶点的潜在意义。
